messages:
alex_infra: Heads up — we rolled the CU12 builder images to ap-southeast GPU pool at 08:12Z and started seeing container-rebuild churn on ~12 nodes. Symptoms: ld.so/GLIBC errors, NVML driver/toolkit mismatch warnings, and intermittent NCCL connect timeouts.

maria_sre: any crash logs? can you paste the first failing container logs?

alex_infra: paste from one of the failing pods:
```
/opt/cuda/compat/libcuda.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2: version `GLIBC_2.34' not found (required by /opt/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12.1)
ERROR: failed to map /opt/cuda/lib64/libnvidia-ml.so.1: undefined symbol: __atomic_load_n
NCCL WARN Connection reset by peer
```

jamal_eng: is this coming from the new base image or the gradual container rebuild? we changed the builder image to gcc13 last week for CI speedups.

yun_runtime: looks like an ABI mismatch — runtime libs in the container are linked against a newer libstdc++/glibc than the host supports. Are we accidentally binding host /usr/lib into the image?

alex_infra: we do mount /lib/modules and /usr/src sometimes for driver builds, but not glibc. However the image build step used ccache and might have baked host toolchain artifacts into layers. suspect gcc13-linked libstdc++ slipped into some images.

maria_sre: any kernel version correlation? I saw a batch of nodes on kernel 6.2 that had different linker paths earlier.

ops-oncall: infra-bot: rebuild-queue spike detected — 50 rebuild jobs in 12m for ap-southeast.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline started: docker-builds/patch-cu12 2026-03-16T08:10Z (50 jobs)

jamal_eng: rolling back images built with gcc13 should stop the churn. short-term fix: pin builder to gcc11 for stable channel. mid-term: make a proper multistage build that produces a fully self-contained runtime.

yun_runtime: short-term mitigations: 1) mark ap-southeast pool as canary-disabled so auto-rollouts skip it; 2) add LD_LIBRARY_PATH and soname checks into the readiness probe; 3) add a job that runs `ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so` in CI matrix.

alex_infra: +1. Also we need to confirm driver req: CU12 needs driver >=535, right? if we have older drivers, that could also explain NVML warnings.

jamal_eng: yes, driver 535+ is recommended for CUDA 12.x. We have a mixed driver fleet — some older baremetal nodes stayed on 525. That mismatch will break some workloads.

maria_sre: cost/ops note — reprovisioning nodes to new driver or spinning replacement nodes will spike allocation and billing. Estimate 3-4 hours of overlapping capacity. Ops, can we absorb that?

ops-oncall: approve a short-term capacity spike. Tag any reprovisioning with billing tag infra-cu12-rollback. I'll notify finance.

jamal_eng: I'll open a PR to pin the builder image to gcc11 for the stable CI images and add a test that runs `readelf -s` to detect SONAME mismatches. assigning @yun_runtime to validate the runtime variants.

yun_runtime: will run quick harness: `docker run --rm --gpus all myorg/base:cu12-gcc11 nvidia-smi && ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so` and report back in 20m.

alex_infra: immediate actions (short list):
- pause rollout to ap-southeast (done)
- add canary-disabled label to ap-southeast pools (in progress)
- revert unstable images to last-known-good built with gcc11 (jamal)
- run host-driver audit for 525 vs 535 (alex + ops)
- draft runbook for rebuild fallout (maria)

maria_sre: drafting runbook now — will include quick checks: `ldd`, `readelf -d`, `strings libnvidia-ml.so | grep SONAME`, and a tiny NCCL connectivity probe. Posting link in 30m.

ops-oncall: scheduling a 30m sync in 15m. :clock1: Everyone involved please join.

alex_infra: thanks. I'll keep updates here — please reply in-thread (thread_ts 2398765432).
